Vaccine trials for zoonotic pathogens have a problem that trials for
human-to-human pathogens do not. Efficacy is measured against incident
infection, and infection arrives from wildlife at times and places nobody can
predict. Ecology is therefore not background to the trial, it is part of its
design.

This is the direction I want my own work to take: using what we know about
reservoirs and about human exposure to make trials of Lassa fever vaccines
answerable, and doing the same for the next priority pathogen.

## Papers

- **A One Health trial design to accelerate Lassa fever vaccines.**
  *Nature Medicine*, 2026. Ecological and social data entering antigen
  selection, site selection and evaluation.
- **Developing transmissible vaccines for animal infections.**
  *Science*, 2024. Design commitments for self-disseminating vaccines, from an
  interdisciplinary workshop.
